clue.text: Actor's second part involves energy in a mixture of languages

indicators.note: second picks out only the second letter of the word Actor's
involves means the part holds the energy letter inside it

parts.note: an actor's part is a role
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A performer's second role demands energy from someone speaking a blend of tongues.
explanation.definitionFit: A creole is a stable language formed from the mixing of two or more others.

clue.text: Better cooking one fattened specially

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo
on means cooking, as food on the stove

explanation.surface: Better cooking suits someone who has been specially fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table.

clue.text: Bullfighter's little scam I'll offer to conceal

indicators.note: to conceal means the letters are held within the run of words

explanation.surface: A matador offers to hide his small swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: Escamillo is the toreador in Bizet's opera Carmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Escamillo is the famous toreador who wins Carmen in Bizet's opera.

clue.text: Represent part of body in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the body part's word is spoken, the letters entered sounding the same

parts.note: a limb is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A speaker portrays a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To limn is to depict or portray in a picture or words.

clue.text: What may be afoot is a cheeky failure

parts.note: flip means flippant or cheeky
a flop is a failure

explanation.surface: Something going on is an impudent fiasco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' reads as 'happening', but here it means literally on a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandal held by a thong between the toes is worn on the foot, hence literally afoot.

clue.text: Two forms of support keeping a person entitled to benefit

indicators.note: keeping means the two supports hold the a between them

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Two kinds of support are given to a beneficiary.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is someone left a legacy in a will, so entitled to benefit.

clue.text: Wildly extravagant academic tie up

parts.note: prof, professor, is an academic
to ligate is to tie up, as a surgeon ties a blood vessel

explanation.surface: An extravagant don ties up the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Profligate means recklessly wasteful or extravagant with money.

clue.text: Stop before Paris, sick to be among the French

indicators.note: to be among means the sick word sits inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A traveller stops on the way to Paris because they feel ill among the French.
explanation.walkthrough: Lille is a French city where Eurostar trains stop before reaching Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a station on the high-speed line from London to Paris, a stop before the capital.

clue.text: Somehow learn pity for what politician follows

indicators.note: somehow signals that the letters are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: A politician somehow learns compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: The policy line set by a political party is what its members are expected to toe.

clue.text: Definitely confirm duke's not using money

parts.note: to ink in a plan is to confirm it definitely, after pencilling it
D is the standard abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A duke confirms that he won't pay in cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying in kind means with goods or services rather than cash.

clue.text: Game includes English bowler

indicators.note: includes means the game's name holds the English letter within it

parts.note: Pac-Man is a classic video game

explanation.surface: A sport features an English bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler who relies on speed is a fast bowler or paceman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bowler who bowls fast is called a paceman, a common term for such players.

clue.text: Iceberg lettuce initially secured by nurseryman

indicators.note: secured by means the initial letter is held inside the nurseryman word

parts.note: a nurseryman is a grower of plants

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of lettuce

explanation.surface: A gardener at a nursery plants out iceberg lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iceberg lettuce' looks like one item, but Iceberg alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small floating iceberg, lower than a berg, is known as a growler.

clue.text: Roll back over motorway, dead

indicators.note: over here means the reversed roll sits all around the motorway letter
back means the roll word is read backwards

parts.note: a bun is a bread roll
M is the British abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A car rolls backwards over the motorway and someone is killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns BUN into NUB, which is split to take in M.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb means without feeling, as a dead limb is.

clue.text: Quieter during homework — the hard stuff starts here

indicators.note: during means the quieter word goes inside the homework abbreviation

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work on one's home
stiller means quieter

explanation.surface: Things go quieter during homework, and then the real hard work begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'homework' suggests school, but it is home improvement; 'the hard stuff' is spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits such as whisky, called the hard stuff, are made at a plant that distils them.

clue.text: Cobbled together, so ensuring preferred result?

definitions.meaning: made roughly with whatever is at hand
a fixed or rigged jury would deliver the verdict someone wants

explanation.definitionFit: Jury-rigged means improvised in makeshift fashion, and read literally suggests a court panel that has been fixed.

clue.text: Here martyrs, led up to centre of gallows, died horribly

indicators.note: horribly signals that the gathered letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the seven-letter gallows

explanation.surface: Martyrs were led to the gallows and died a horrible death.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tolpuddle Martyrs were Dorset farm labourers transported to Australia in 1834 for forming a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorset village gives its name to the famous union martyrs of 1834.

clue.text: Bitter cynic in ripped tee shirts

indicators.note: ripped signals that the letters are torn up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sour cynic is seen in torn T-shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: Thersites is the foul-mouthed railing Greek in Homer's Iliad and Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida.
explanation.definitionFit: Thersites is the scurrilous, sneering Greek soldier in the Iliad, a byword for bitter mockery.

clue.text: Tenor's fifty-first performance

definitions.note: the clue's 'Tenor's' stands for 'tenor is', the answer being a tenor

parts.note: a gig is a performance
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral one, and first means number one

explanation.surface: A singer gives his fifty-first concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Beniamino Gigli was a celebrated Italian operatic tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: Beniamino Gigli is one of the most famous Italian operatic tenors of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Boy, one grabbed by fearsome beast, is a fighter

indicators.note: grabbed by means the boy and one go inside the beast

parts.note: gator, short for alligator, is a fearsome beast
a lad is a boy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A boy is seized by a terrifying animal, yet fights back.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator was a Roman who fought in the arena, a fighter by trade.

clue.text: Point to very thin black

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
bony means very thin, skin and bone

explanation.surface: Someone notes how very thin a black thing is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a deep black colour, named after the dark wood.

clue.text: Making a turn right, gripped by some fury on the road

indicators.note: gripped by means the right letter is held inside the phrase for some

parts.note: a bit means some
road rage is fury on the road, giving rage

explanation.surface: A driver turning right is caught up in road rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a turn' looks like driving, but a turn is a trading profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbitrage is buying and selling across markets to profit from price gaps, making a turn on them.

clue.text: American city sounds more imposing

indicators.note: sounds signals that the comparative is spoken, matching a word spelt differently

parts.note: more august means more imposing, giving the comparative auguster

explanation.surface: A US city seems grander.
explanation.walkthrough: Augusta is the capital of Maine and a city in Georgia, home of the golf Masters.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is a city in the US, the capital of Maine and also a city in Georgia.

clue.text: I go red all over? More the opposite

indicators.note: all over signals that the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: to blush is to go red

explanation.surface: Someone flushes red all over and is told it is quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposite of red, as in politics, is blue, so 'More the opposite' means tending to blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tending towards blue, the colour set against red, as in British party politics.

clue.text: Unarguable evidence such a jacket needs arm

parts.note: a smoking jacket is a type of jacket
a gun is an arm, a weapon

explanation.surface: A garment like that needs a sleeve, says the evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof that clearly shows guilt is called a smoking gun, as if found in the culprit's hand.

clue.text: Wood area surrounds small city

indicators.note: surrounds means the wood and area letters go all around the small letter

parts.note: oak is a wood

explanation.surface: Woodland surrounds a small town.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port city in Japan.

clue.text: Show disapproval of interference

definitions.meaning: background noise interfering with a signal

explanation.definitionFit: A hiss is both a sound of disapproval and the static that disturbs a broadcast.

clue.text: Flight of birds elegant at first in film

indicators.note: in means the first letter goes inside the film word

parts.note: a skin is a thin film or layer

indicators.note: at first picks the first letter of elegant

explanation.surface: A flock of birds looks elegant at the start of a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' suggests cinema, but it is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is a flock of wild geese in flight.

clue.text: A foolish person turns up having lost pet cat

indicators.note: turns up, in a down clue, means the letters are read bottom to top
having lost means the word pet is taken off the end

parts.note: a muppet is slang for a foolish person
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fool appears after losing a beloved cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet cat' reads as one phrase, but pet is removed from A MUPPET, leaving AMUP, which 'turns up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma is a large wild American cat, also called the cougar.

clue.text: Race to drop back when this is fired?

definitions.text: Race to drop back when this is fired?

parts.note: to tear is to race or rush

indicators.note: back means the drop word is read backwards

parts.note: to sag is to drop

explanation.surface: Rioters run and fall back when this weapon is used against them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a crowd fleeing when the police fire tear gas canisters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear gas canisters fired into a crowd make people run and fall back.

clue.text: Move quickly to sink

definitions.meaning: to ... a ship is to sink it deliberately

explanation.definitionFit: Scuttle means both to scurry and to deliberately sink a vessel.

clue.text: Not be persuaded to buy Irishman a drink

parts.note: to stand someone a drink is to buy it for them
Pat is a typical Irish name used for an Irishman

explanation.surface: Someone declines to buy a pint for an Irish friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker, standing pat means keeping one's hand unchanged, hence holding firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand pat is to hold firm and refuse to change one's position.

clue.text: In Hastings, for example, battled endlessly against leader of Normans

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the battle word is dropped

parts.note: warred means battled

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter of Normans

explanation.surface: At Hastings the English fought on and on against the Norman leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface means the 1066 battle, but Hastings is Warren Hastings, the first Governor-General of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Warren is the first name of Hastings, the eighteenth-century Governor-General of India.
